title: Simple lisse support reduction before decomposing geometric constituents
statement: Let $k_0$ be a finite field, $\ell$ an invertible prime, $X/k_0$ a smooth affine finite-type scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and $V$ an irreducible nonzero lisse source Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Let $x,y$ be finite points with nonzero stalks. There exist a finite extension $k_1/k_0$, a smooth geometrically connected separated affine finite-type scheme $C/k_1$ of constant relative dimension $d>0$ and irreducible geometric fiber, an exact functor $R$ from source Weil sheaves on $X$ to source Weil sheaves on $C$, and a morphism $c:C\to X$ over the field extension, such that $R(V)$ is arithmetically irreducible lisse. The functor preserves lissity and has pointwise power transport along $c$ [def-zl-source-constant-field-restriction]. Both $x$ and $y$ have finite-point lifts on $C$. No geometric direct-sum decomposition or orbit comparison of summands is asserted.

proof.text: Choose the geometrically connected clopen support C₀ over its constant field k₁, of dimension d≥0, and the two marked-point lifts. On this supplied component use native clopen return restriction to obtain the exact functor R₀, its lissity and pointwise transport, and simplicity of R₀(V). The lift of x and its original nonzero stalk discharge the nonzero restriction hypothesis.

proof.text: Always replace C₀ by A=𝔸¹_C₀. The affine-line simplicity theorem proves that p*R₀(V) stays simple lisse. The projection has dimension one, so A has dimension 1+d>0. It is affine, smooth, geometrically connected, separated and finite type. Smooth geometric connectedness gives irreducibility of its geometric fiber. Compose R₀ with exact native pullback p*; the zero section lifts the two marked points.

proof.text: Prove pointwise power transport for ordinary native pullback using the existing geometric stalk-comparison equivalences, Frobenius iteration, and the residue-degree tower. Compose it with the component-return transport: exponents multiply and Frobenius-module equivalences commute with taking powers. Assemble all witnesses and the base-field square. This is complete Lean glue, with no eigenline or point-flag step.

theorem exists_simple_lisse_support_model
    {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsAffine X]
    [Smooth (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    (V : WeilSheaf k₀ l X) (hV : V.IsIrreducibleLisse)
    (x y : X.finitePoints)
    (hx : Nontrivial (V.stalk x).carrier) (hy : Nontrivial (V.stalk y).carrier) :
    ∃ (k₁ : Type u) (_ : Field k₁) (_ : Finite k₁) (_ : Algebra k₀ k₁)
      (_ : Fact (ringChar k₁ ≠ l)) (d : ℕ) (C : Scheme.{u})
      (_ : C.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁))) (_ : IsAffine C)
      (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : GeometricallyConnected (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : IsSeparated (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : LocallyOfFiniteType (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : QuasiCompact (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)))
      (_ : IrreducibleSpace (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)).geometricFiber)
      (R : WeilSheaf k₀ l X ⥤ WeilSheaf k₁ l C)
      (_ : PreservesFiniteLimits R) (_ : PreservesFiniteColimits R) (c : C ⟶ X),
      0 < d ∧ (R.obj V).IsIrreducibleLisse ∧
      (∀ F : WeilSheaf k₀ l X, F.IsLisse → (R.obj F).IsLisse) ∧
      HasPointwisePowerTransport R c ∧
      c ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)) =
        (C ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₁)) ≫
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k₀ k₁)) ∧
      ∃ s t : C.finitePoints, c s.1 = x.1 ∧ c t.1 = y.1
